shortDescription: Manage bits and pieces of XML files or strings

options.name: add_children
options.description: Add additional child-element(s) to a selected element for a given O(xpath). Child elements must be given in a list and each item may be either a string (for example C(children=ansible) to add an empty C(<ansible/>) child element), or a hash where the key is an element name and the value is the element value. This parameter requires O(xpath) to be set.

options.name: attribute
options.description: The attribute to select when using parameter O(value). This is a string, not prepended with V(@).

options.name: backup
options.description: Create a backup file including the timestamp information so you can get the original file back if you somehow clobbered it incorrectly.

options.name: content
options.description: Search for a given O(xpath) and get content. This parameter requires O(xpath) to be set.

options.name: count
options.description: Search for a given O(xpath) and provide the count of any matches. This parameter requires O(xpath) to be set.

options.name: create_if_missing
options.description: When using O(value) and the O(xpath) matches no nodes, create the node. When set to V(false), a no-match is silently ignored instead of creating a new node.

options.name: huge_tree
options.description: Disable libxml2 security restrictions on XML node size or document depth, allowing processing of very large XML files. This option should only be activated when needed, as it disables internal safety limits.

options.name: input_type
options.description: Type of input for O(add_children) and O(set_children).

options.name: insertafter
options.description: Add additional child-element(s) after the last selected element for a given O(xpath). Child elements must be given in a list and each item may be either a string (for example C(children=ansible) to add an empty C(<ansible/>) child element), or a hash where the key is an element name and the value is the element value. This parameter requires O(xpath) to be set.

options.name: insertbefore
options.description: Add additional child-element(s) before the first selected element for a given O(xpath). Child elements must be given in a list and each item may be either a string (for example C(children=ansible) to add an empty C(<ansible/>) child element), or a hash where the key is an element name and the value is the element value. This parameter requires O(xpath) to be set.

options.name: namespaces
options.description: The namespace C(prefix:uri) mapping for the XPath expression. Needs to be a C(dict), not a C(list) of items.

options.name: path
options.description: Path to the file to operate on. This file must exist ahead of time. This parameter is required, unless O(xmlstring) is given.

options.name: pretty_print
options.description: Pretty print XML output.

options.name: print_match
options.description: Search for a given O(xpath) and print out any matches. This parameter requires O(xpath) to be set.

options.name: set_children
options.description: Set the child-element(s) of a selected element for a given O(xpath). Removes any existing children. Child elements must be specified as in O(add_children). This parameter requires O(xpath) to be set.

options.name: state
options.description: Set or remove an xpath selection (node(s), attribute(s)).

options.name: strip_cdata_tags
options.description: Remove CDATA tags surrounding text values. Note that this might break your XML file if text values contain characters that could be interpreted as XML.

options.name: value
options.description: Desired state of the selected attribute. Either a string, or to unset a value, the Python V(None) keyword (YAML Equivalent, V(null)). Elements default to no value (but present). Attributes default to an empty string.

options.name: xmlstring
options.description: A string containing XML on which to operate. This parameter is required, unless O(path) is given.

options.name: xpath
options.description: A valid XPath expression describing the item(s) you want to operate on. Operates on the document root, V(/), by default.
